torvosaurus:enwiki:12.title: Torvosaurus (Fauna and habitat in North America)

torvosaurus:enwiki:15.title: Torvosaurus (Fauna and habitat in South America)

facts.statement: Torvosaurus lived during the Middle to Late Jurassic periods, specifically from the Callovian to Tithonian ages.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Middle - Late Jurassic (Callovian to Tithonian),

facts.statement: The genus Torvosaurus was named by Peter Malcolm Galton and James Alvin Jensen in 1979.
facts.quote: authority: Galton & Jensen, 1979

facts.statement: The type species Torvosaurus tanneri was formally named in 1979.
facts.quote: In 1979, the type species Torvosaurus tanneri was named.

facts.statement: Torvosaurus tanneri measured around 9 meters long and weighed approximately 2 to 2.4 metric tons, making it one of the largest terrestrial carnivores in Late Jurassic North America.
facts.quote: Measuring around 9 m long and weighing approximately 2 - 2.4 MT, T. tanneri was among the largest terrestrial carnivores in North America during the Late Jurassic.

facts.statement: Specimens of Torvosaurus gurneyi have been measured up to 10 meters in length and 4 to 5 metric tons in body mass.
facts.quote: Specimens of Torvosaurus gurneyi were measured up to 10 m in length and 4 - 5 MT in body mass.

facts.statement: The first remains referable to Torvosaurus were discovered in 1899 by Elmer Riggs in the Freeze-out Hills of southeastern Wyoming.
facts.quote: The first discovered remains referable to Torvosaurus were discovered in 1899 by Elmer Riggs in the "Freeze-out Hills" of southeastern Wyoming, 11 mi northwest of Medicine Bow.

facts.statement: Remains from Tanzania were named Megalosaurus ingens by Werner Janensch in 1920 based on a 12 cm tooth, later reclassified as a probable member of Torvosaurus.
facts.quote: More remains of a large theropod that is now believed to have been Torvosaurus were discovered in the Tendaguru Formation of Tanzania and was named "Megalosaurus" ingens by Werner Janensch in 1920, based on the specimen MB R 1050, a 12 cm tooth from German East Africa (now Tanzania).

facts.statement: Teeth of a Torvosaurus member were described from the Tacuarembó Formation of Uruguay by Soto et al. in 2020.
facts.quote: Soto et al. (2020) described teeth of a member of the genus Torvosaurus from the Tacuarembó Formation of Uruguay.

facts.statement: A gigantic theropod thumb claw was discovered in 1971 by Vivian Jones at the Calico Gulch Quarry in Moffat County, Colorado.
facts.quote: In 1971, Vivian Jones of Delta, Colorado, in the Calico Gulch Quarry in Moffat County, discovered a single gigantic thumb claw of a theropod.

facts.statement: Torvosaurus tanneri was named and described in 1979 by Peter Malcolm Galton and James Alvin Jensen.
facts.quote: The type species Torvosaurus tanneri was named and described in 1979 by Peter Malcolm Galton and Jensen.

facts.statement: The specific name tanneri honors Nathan Eldon Tanner, a first counselor in the First Presidency of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.
facts.quote: The specific name tanneri comes from the, first counselor in the First Presidency of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, Nathan Eldon Tanner.

facts.statement: In 1985, James Alvin Jensen reported additional Torvosaurus material, including the first skull elements.
facts.quote: In 1985, Jensen could report a considerable amount of additional material, among it being the first skull elements.

facts.statement: The holotype and paratype material of Torvosaurus represented at least three individuals: two adults and one juvenile.
facts.quote: The holotype and paratypes represented at least three individuals, these being two adults and a juvenile.

facts.statement: In 1992, fossils containing skull, shoulder girdle, pelvic, and rib elements were found at Como Bluff in Wyoming.
facts.quote: In 1992, fossils of a large theropod found at Como Bluff in Wyoming contained skull, shoulder girdle, pelvic, and rib elements.

facts.statement: Most researchers now consider Edmarka rex and the informal name Brontoraptor to be junior synonyms of Torvosaurus tanneri.
facts.quote: Most researchers now regard both Edmarka rex and "Brontoraptor" as junior synonyms of Torvosaurus tanneri.

facts.statement: A 55% complete, undescribed Torvosaurus specimen nicknamed 'Elvis' was discovered in 2012 at the Skull Creek Quarry in Colorado.
facts.quote: In 2012, a still undescribed, 55% complete specimen was discovered in Colorado in the Skull Creek Quarry, which is an exposure of the Morrison Formation.

facts.statement: The specimen nicknamed 'Elvis' is the most complete Torvosaurus specimen found to date.
facts.quote: It is the most complete specimen of Torvosaurus found to date.

facts.statement: It is debated whether teeth from Tanzania and Uruguay belong to Torvosaurus, as some researchers consider them undiagnostic and similar to other theropods like carcharodontosaurids.
facts.quote: However, Rauhut et al. (2020) consider the teeth to be undiagnostic, being coherent in size and shape with a variety of other theropods (including carcharodontosaurids), thus considering their attribution to the genus to be problematic.

facts.statement: In 2000, Octávio Mateus and Miguel Telles Antunes referred Portuguese material to Torvosaurus sp.
facts.quote: In 2000, material from Portugal was referred to a Torvosaurus sp. by Octávio Mateus and Miguel Telles Antunes.

facts.statement: In 2006, fossils from the Lourinhã Formation in Portugal were assigned to Torvosaurus tanneri.
facts.quote: In 2006, fossils from the Portuguese Lourinhã Formation were referred to Torvosaurus tanneri.

facts.statement: Matthew Carrano and colleagues concluded in 2012 that Portuguese material could not be identified more precisely than Torvosaurus sp.
facts.quote: In 2012, however, Matthew Carrano and colleagues concluded that this material could not be more precisely determined than a Torvosaurus sp.

facts.statement: Eggs with and without embryos were reported from Portugal in 2013 and 2014 and referred to Torvosaurus.
facts.quote: In 2013 and 2014, eggs with and without embryos were reported from Portugal and referred to Torvosaurus.

facts.statement: The Portuguese species was named Torvosaurus gurneyi in 2014 to honor James Gurney, the creator of the Dinotopia book series.
facts.quote: The species from Portugal was named T. gurneyi in honor of James Gurney in 2014, the creator of the Dinotopia series of books.

facts.statement: Torvosaurus gurneyi is the largest named theropod from Europe, though a Spanish vertebra from the Vega Formation is about 15% larger.
facts.quote: It is the largest named theropod known from Europe, although an isolated anterior caudal vertebra from the Vega Formation in Spain, which may belong to Torvosaurus or a closely related taxon, is about 15% larger than the one found on T. gurneyi.

facts.statement: The German maxilla represents the earliest record of the genus and suggests megalosaurines may have originated in Europe or that Europe was a biogeographical hub for them.
facts.quote: This is the record of the genus and suggests that megalosaurines originated in Europe, or at least that Europe was a biogeographical turntable for them from the Middle to the early Late Jurassic.

facts.statement: Teeth likely belonging to Torvosaurus were described in 2016 from the Kimmeridgian of Germany.
facts.quote: In 2016 teeth regarded as likely coming from Torvosaurus were described from the Kimmeridgian of Germany.

facts.statement: Subsequent studies estimate adult Torvosaurus reached 9 to 11 meters in length and weighed up to 2 to 4.4 metric tons.
facts.quote: Subsequent studies have estimated that adults reached 9-11 m in length, and weighed up to 2 - 4.4 MT.

facts.statement: Torvosaurus gurneyi is estimated to have measured 10 to 12 meters in length and weighed 4 to 5 metric tons.
facts.quote: T. gurneyi is estimated to have measured 10-12 m in length and weighed 4 - 5 MT.

facts.statement: The premaxilla of Torvosaurus bore three flat teeth oriented outwards, with the front edge of each crown overlapping the rear edge of the preceding one.
facts.quote: The frontmost snout bone, the premaxilla, bore three rather flat teeth oriented somewhat outwards with the front edge of the teeth crown overlapping the outer side of the rear edge of the preceding crown.

facts.statement: The maxilla of Torvosaurus was tall and bore at least eleven long teeth.
facts.quote: The maxilla was tall and bore at least eleven rather long teeth.

facts.statement: Like other megalosaurids, the largest teeth in Torvosaurus were located in the second to sixth maxillary alveoli.
facts.quote: Like other megalosaurids, the largest teeth in the mouth of Torvosaurus were in the second to sixth maxillary alveoli.

facts.statement: The lacrimal bone of Torvosaurus had a distinctive horn on top and a broad lower end in side view.
facts.quote: The lacrimal bone had a distinctive lacrimal horn on top. Its lower end was broad in side view.

facts.statement: The eye socket of Torvosaurus was tall with a pointed lower end.
facts.quote: The eye socket was tall with a pointed lower end.

facts.statement: The jugal bone of Torvosaurus was long and transversely thin.
facts.quote: The jugal was long and transversely thin.

facts.statement: The preserved maxilla of Torvosaurus gurneyi is 63 cm long, indicating a total length of 71 cm after accounting for missing parts.
facts.quote: The maxilla of T. gurneyi is 63 cm in length as preserved but is missing 8 cm of the ventroposterior rim. This indicates the total length of T. gurneyi maxilla is 71 cm in length.

facts.statement: The holotype of Torvosaurus gurneyi had teeth measuring 10.6 to 11.6 cm in crown height.
facts.quote: The teeth of T. gurneyi were much bigger however, the holotype of T. gurneyi had teeth that measured from 10.6-11.6 cm in crown height.

facts.statement: The largest teeth of Torvosaurus gurneyi were 15 cm in crown height.
facts.quote: The largest teeth of T. gurneyi were 15 cm in crown height.

facts.statement: Torvosaurus gurneyi possesses the largest teeth of any theropod found in the Lourinhã Formation.
facts.quote: T. gurneyi has the largest teeth of any theropod in the Lourinhã Formation.

facts.statement: Among large theropods in the Lourinhã Formation, only Torvosaurus teeth exceed 7.5 cm in crown height.
facts.quote: Amongst the large theropods of the Lourinhã Formation, only the teeth of Torvosaurus exceed 7.5 cm in crown height.

facts.statement: Both the neck and front dorsal vertebrae of Torvosaurus had relatively flexible ball-in-socket joints.
facts.quote: Both the neck vertebrae and the front dorsal vertebrae had relatively flexible ball-in-socket joints.

facts.statement: The toes of Torvosaurus were relatively short compared to other theropods, featuring short and stout pedal phalanges.
facts.quote: The toes of Torvosaurus are noted as being relatively short compared to other theropods, with short and stout pedal phalanges.

facts.statement: The entire arm of Torvosaurus was very strong but somewhat short.
facts.quote: The whole of the arm was very strong, but somewhat short.

facts.statement: It is uncertain whether the thumb claw of Torvosaurus was especially enlarged.
facts.quote: Whether the thumb claw was especially enlarged is uncertain.

facts.statement: The pelvis of Torvosaurus was massively built, with bone skirts between the pubic bones and ischia contacting to form a vaulted closed underside.
facts.quote: The pelvis as a whole was massively built, with the bone skirts between the pubic bones and the ischia contacting each other and forming a vaulted closed underside.

facts.statement: Torvosaurus was first classified as a megalosaurid in 1979, a classification that remains the current consensus.
facts.quote: When first described in 1979 by Galton and Jensen, Torvosaurus was classified as a megalosaurid, which is the current consensus.

facts.statement: In 1985, Jensen assigned Torvosaurus to its own family, Torvosauridae.
facts.quote: In 1985, Jensen assigned Torvosaurus to a family of its own, Torvosauridae.

facts.statement: Although a close relative of Megalosaurus, Torvosaurus appears to be more advanced or apomorphic.
facts.quote: Though a close relative of Megalosaurus, Torvosaurus is seemingly more advanced, or apomorphic.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests megalosaurines may have originated in Europe or that Europe served as a biogeographical hub for them from the Middle to early Late Jurassic.
facts.quote: This is the record of the genus and suggests that megalosaurines originated in Europe, or at least that Europe was a biogeographical turntable for them from the Middle to the early Late Jurassic.

facts.statement: Eggs with and without embryos referred to Torvosaurus were reported from Portugal in 2013 and 2014.
facts.quote: In 2013 and 2014, eggs with and without embryos were reported from Portugal and referred to Torvosaurus.

facts.statement: One describer of Torvosaurus gurneyi argued that giant vertebrae from the Vega Formation likely belong to T. gurneyi, though this is debated.
facts.quote: One of the describers of T.gurneyi argued the giant vertebrae from the Vega Formation likely does belong to T.gurneyi.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the lower number of maxillary teeth in Torvosaurus gurneyi is a real distinction or an artifact of preservation, as the exact count remains unknown.
facts.quote: However, later examination of a new right maxilla, probably belonging to the same individual as the holotype of T. gurneyi, has determined that, while the two species can be distinguished based on the morphology of the maxillary medial wall and interdental plates, the supposedly lower number of maxillary teeth in the Portuguese form may be an artifact of preservation, since it is not possible to know the exact number of teeth in the complete maxilla at the moment.

facts.statement: Torvosaurus possesses fused interdental plates in its jaw.
facts.quote: The presence of fused interdental plates

facts.statement: The Torvosaurus egg clutch was discovered in 2005 by Dutch amateur fossil-hunter Aart Walen in the Lourinhã Formation, Western Portugal, dating to the Tithonian age of the Jurassic (152 to 145 million years ago).
facts.quote: This discovery was made in 2005 by the Dutch amateur fossil-hunter Aart Walen at the Lourinhã Formation in Western Portugal in fluvial overbank sediments that are considered to be from the Tithonian age of the Jurassic, approximately 152 to 145 million years ago.

facts.statement: The Torvosaurus embryos found in Portugal are the only known basal theropod embryos.
facts.quote: these are the only basal theropod embryos known

facts.statement: The highly porous eggshells of Torvosaurus indicate that the eggs were buried in the substrate for incubation, similar to modern sea turtles.
facts.quote: the eggshells are highly porous, allowing efficient gaseous exchange between the external and internal media, thus indicating the eggs were buried for incubation within substrate in a manner similar to modern seaturtles.

facts.statement: All documented Torvosaurus specimens from the Morrison Formation appear to be similarly sized adult individuals, though the lack of immature individuals may be due to various factors.
facts.quote: All documented Torvosaurus specimens from the Morrison Formation are from similarly sized, likely adult individuals and the lack of immature individuals may be explained by many factors, none of which are mutually exclusive.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Torvosaurus tanneri (BYU 2002) was recovered from the Dry Mesa Quarry in the Brushy Basin Member of the Morrison Formation in Montrose County, Colorado.
facts.quote: The type specimen of Torvosaurus tanneri, BYU 2002, was recovered in the Dry Mesa Quarry of the Brushy Basin Member of the Morrison Formation in Montrose County, Colorado.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Torvosaurus tanneri was collected by James A. Jensen and Kenneth Stadtman in 1972 from sandstone deposited during the Tithonian and Kimmeridgian ages (153 to 148 million years ago).
facts.quote: The specimen was collected by James A. Jensen and Kenneth Stadtman in 1972 in medium-grained, coarse sandstone that was deposited during the Tithonian and Kimmeridgian ages of the Jurassic, approximately 153 to 148 million years ago.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Torvosaurus tanneri is housed in the collection of Brigham Young University in Provo, Utah.
facts.quote: This specimen is housed in the collection of Brigham Young University in Provo, Utah.

facts.statement: Studies suggest the paleoenvironment of the Morrison Formation included rivers flowing into a basin with a giant saline alkaline lake and extensive wetlands.
facts.quote: Studies suggest that the paleoenvironment of this section of the Morrison Formation included rivers that flowed from the west into a basin that contained a giant, saline alkaline lake and there were extensive wetlands in the vicinity.

facts.statement: The Dry Mesa Quarry has produced remains of diverse species including sauropods like Apatosaurus and Camarasaurus, theropods like Allosaurus and Ceratosaurus, and ornithischians like Stegosaurus.
facts.quote: The Dry Mesa Quarry has produced the remains of the sauropods Apatosaurus, Brachiosaurus, Diplodocus, Barosaurus, Supersaurus, and Camarasaurus, the iguanodonts Camptosaurus and Dryosaurus, and the theropods Allosaurus, Tanycolagreus, Koparion, Stokesosaurus, Ceratosaurus, and Ornitholestes, as well as Othnielosaurus, Gargoyleosaurus, and Stegosaurus.

facts.statement: In the Callovian-aged Ornatenton Formation, Torvosaurus lived alongside the closely related and large Wiehenvenator.
facts.quote: The Ornatenton Formation is a Callovian aged shallow marine deposit, within the formation Torvosaurus was sympatric with the closely related and also large Wiehenvenator.

facts.statement: The Lourinhã Formation, where Torvosaurus fossils are found, dates to the Kimmeridgian–Tithonian ages and features a coastal environment with strong marine influence.
facts.quote: The Lourinhã Formation is Kimmeridgian–Tithonian in age. The environment is coastal and therefore has a strong marine influence.

facts.statement: Torvosaurus appears to have been the top predator in the Lourinhã Formation, living alongside European Allosaurus, Ceratosaurus, Stegosaurus, and Camptosaurus.
facts.quote: Torvosaurus appears to be the top predator here. It lived alongside the European species of Allosaurus (A. europaeus), Ceratosaurus, Stegosaurus, and presumably Camptosaurus.

facts.statement: In the Lourinhã Formation, Lusotitan was the largest sauropod, alongside diplodocids like Dinheirosaurus and Lourinhasaurus.
facts.quote: Lusotitan was the largest sauropod in the region, while the diplodocids Dinheirosaurus and Lourinhasaurus were also present.

facts.statement: Possible Torvosaurus material from the Tendaguru Formation is found in sandstone interpreted as tidal flat deposits.
facts.quote: The small-scale trough and ripple cross-bedded fine-grained sandstone at the base of the Upper Dinosaur Member of the Tendaguru Formation, of which possible Torvosaurus material is known from, is interpreted as tidal flat deposits.

facts.statement: The environment of the Tendaguru Formation included stagnant water bodies like small lakes and ponds, as well as a freshwater depositional environment near the sea.
facts.quote: Stagnant water bodies, such as small lakes and ponds, were present and a freshwater depositional environment close to the sea was also probably present.

facts.statement: Torvosaurus coexisted with theropods like Allosaurus tendagurensis and Ceratosaurus roechlingi, and ornithischians like Dysalotosaurus and Kentrosaurus in the Tendaguru Formation.
facts.quote: The theropods it coexisted with were Allosaurus tendagurensis, Ceratosaurus roechlingi, Elaphrosaurus, Labrosaurus stechowi, Ostafrikasaurus, Veterupristisaurus (of which it would have possibly competed with to be top predator), a possible abelisauroid, and an indeterminate megalosauroid, while the ornithischians it coexisted with were Dysalotosaurus and Kentrosaurus.

facts.statement: It is debated whether immature Torvosaurus individuals occupied different ecological niches or were prey for larger predators, explaining their scarcity in the fossil record.
facts.quote: Immature individuals may also have occupied a different ecological niche from adults in habitats where their remains were likely to preserve as fossils and they may have been the prey of choice of larger predators as well.

facts.statement: Torvosaurus lived between the late Middle Jurassic and late Upper Jurassic, from 165 to 148 million years ago.
facts.quote: que vivió entre finales período Jurásico Medio y finales del Jurásico Superior, entre 165 a 148 millones de años

facts.statement: Torvosaurus fossils have been found in what is now Europe, North America, Africa, and South America.
facts.quote: en lo que hoy es Europa, Norteamérica, África y Sudamérica

facts.statement: Confirmed Torvosaurus remains have been found in the Morrison Formation of the United States and the Lourinhã Formation of Portugal.
facts.quote: Sus restos se han encontrado tanto en la Formación Morrison de Estados Unidos como en la Formación Lourinhã de Portugal

facts.statement: The type species Torvosaurus tanneri was named in 1979.
facts.quote: En 1979 se nombró a la especie tipo Torvosaurus tanneri

facts.statement: Torvosaurus tanneri was a large, robust, bipedal carnivore that could grow to nearly 10 meters in length.
facts.quote: T. tanneri era un carnívoro bípedo grande, de constitución robusta que podía crecer a una longitud cercana a los 10 metros

facts.statement: Based on bone morphology, Torvosaurus is believed to have had short but very powerful arms.
facts.quote: Basándose en la morfología ósea de Torvosaurus, se cree que tenía brazos cortos pero muy poderosos

facts.statement: Torvosaurus and Ceratosaurus likely preferred waterways and had lower, sinuous bodies suited for forest and underbrush terrain.
facts.quote: Torvosaurus and Ceratosaurus may have preferred to be active around waterways and had lower, more sinuous, bodies that would have given them an advantage in forest and underbrush terrains

facts.statement: Torvosaurus may have been specialized in opening and dismembering exceptionally large sauropod carcasses due to its large skull, teeth, and powerful body.
facts.quote: Torvosaurus, with its large skull and teeth and large, powerful, and lithe body may have been specialized in opening up and dismembering exceptionally large sauropod carcasses

facts.statement: Evidence suggests Allosaurus was a potential food item for other carnivores, indicated by bite marks on its pubic foot likely made by Ceratosaurus or Torvosaurus.
facts.quote: Allosaurus was itself a potential food item to other carnivores, as illustrated by an Allosaurus pubic foot marked by the teeth of another theropod, probably Ceratosaurus or Torvosaurus

facts.statement: It is debated whether bite marks on Allosaurus represent a separate large taxon like Torvosaurus or evidence of cannibalism within Allosaurus.
facts.quote: The result either increases the known diversity of the site based on ichnological evidence alone or represents powerful evidence of cannibalism in Allosaurus

facts.statement: Torvosaurus is classified in the family Megalosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Megalosauridae

facts.statement: Torvosaurus belongs to the subfamily Megalosaurinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Megalosaurinae

facts.statement: Torvosaurus gurneyi is a species described by Hendrickx and Mateus in 2014.
facts.quote: Torvosaurus gurneyi Hendrickx & Mateus, 2014

facts.statement: Torvosaurus ingens is a species described by Soto and colleagues in 2020.
facts.quote: Torvosaurus ingens Soto et al, 2020

facts.statement: Bite marks on Allosaurus and Mymoorapelta were found in the Upper Jurassic Mygatt-Moore Quarry alongside other feeding traces.
facts.quote: Bite marks on Allosaurus and Mymoorapelta remains were found among other bones with feeding traces in the Upper Jurassic Mygatt-Moore Quarry

facts.statement: Torvosaurus was an enormous predator with an estimated maximum body length of 10 meters and a mass of 4 to 5 tonnes for both T. tanneri and T. gurneyi.
facts.quote: Torvosaurus fue un enorme depredador, con una longitud corporal máxima estimada en 10 metros y una masa de 4 a 5 toneladas tanto para T. tanneri como T. gurneyi

facts.statement: The synonym Edmarka rex was named because it was assumed to rival Tyrannosaurus rex in length.
facts.quote: El sinónimo Edmarka rex fue nombrado porque se supuso que rivalizaría con Tyrannosaurus rex en longitud.

facts.statement: Claims based on incomplete remains of Edmarka rex and "Brontoraptor" suggest the American species T. tanneri could reach lengths of up to 12 meters and a mass of over 4 tonnes.
facts.quote: Se han realizado afirmaciones que indican tamaños aún mayores para la especie americana T. tanneri de hasta 12 metros de largo y más de 4 toneladas con base en restos incompletos de Edmarka rex y "Brontoraptor".

facts.statement: Discovered remains of T. tanneri indicate that adults reached a length of 9 meters and a body mass of approximately 2 tonnes.
facts.quote: los restos descubiertos de T. tanneri indica que alcanzaron el tamaño adulto a los 9 metros de largo y aproximadamente 2 toneladas de masa corporal.

facts.statement: Based on the maxilla size, the estimated skull length for the Portuguese specimen is 108 centimeters.
facts.quote: Basado en esto la estimación para el espécimen portugués es de un cráneo de 108 cm.

facts.statement: The premaxilla at the front of the snout has three flattened teeth oriented slightly outward, with the front edge of the crown overlapping the outer side of the preceding crown.
facts.quote: El hueso más al frente en el hocico, el premaxilar, tiene tres dientes aplanados orientados ligeramente hacia afuera con el borde frontal de la corona dental solapándose con el lado externo de la corona precedente.

facts.statement: The upper jaw was high and possessed at least eleven elongated teeth.
facts.quote: El maxilar era alto y tenía al menos once dientes alargados.

facts.statement: The lacrimal bone had a distinctive horn on its upper part, while its lower end was wide in lateral view.
facts.quote: El hueso lacrimal tenía un distintivo cuerno en la parte superior; su extremo inferior es ancho en vista lateral.

facts.statement: The lower front side of the quadrate bone was hollowed out by a tear-shaped depression where it contacted the quadratojugal bone.
facts.quote: La parte inferior del lado frontal del hueso cuadrado estaba ahuecado por una depresión en forma de lágrima, la superficie de contacto con el hueso cuadratoyugal.

facts.statement: The base of the tail was rigid in the vertical plane due to neural spines that were high and very wide in lateral view.
facts.quote: La base de la cola era rígida en el plano vertical por espinas neurales que eran altas y muy anchas en vista lateral.

facts.statement: The complete pelvis had a massive constitution, with bony flaps between the pubis and ischium contacting each other to form a closed vault-like lower part.
facts.quote: La pelvis completa tenía una constitución masiva, con faldones de hueso entre los pubis y los isquiones contactándose entre sí y formando una parte inferior en forma de bóveda cerrada.

facts.statement: Torvosaurus is distinguished by the presence of fused interdental plates.
facts.quote: La presencia de placas interdentales fusionadas.

facts.statement: The puboischiadic plate is highly ossified, with paired bony plates on both sides connecting and closing the lower part of the pelvis.
facts.quote: La placa puboisquiática está muy osificada (las placas óseas pares, en ambos lados, se conectan y cierran en la parte inferior de la pelvis.

facts.statement: A transverse fenestra is located in the neural arch of dorsal vertebrae in front of the hypophysis.
facts.quote: Una fenestra transversa se sitúa en el arco neural de las vértebras dorsales en frents del hiposfeno

facts.statement: Edmarka rex was named as a new genus and species for a theropod from Como Bluff, Wyoming in 1992 by Robert Bakker, Donald Kralis, James Siegwarth, and James Filla.
facts.quote: Edmarka rex fue nombrado como un nuevo género y especie para un terópodo de Como Bluff, Wyoming en 1992 por Robert Bakker, Donald Kralis, James Siegwarth y James Filla.

facts.statement: Another Wyoming specimen was given the informal name "Brontoraptor" by some of the same researchers in 1996.
facts.quote: A otro espécimen de Wyoming se le dio el nombre informal de "Brontoraptor" por parte de algunos de los mismos investigadores en 1996.

facts.statement: Torvosaurus was described and named by Peter M. Galton and James A. Jensen in 1979 with the type species Torvosaurus tanneri.
facts.quote: Torvosaurus fue descrito y nombrado por Peter M. Galton y James A. Jensen en 1979 con la especie tipo Torvosaurus tanneri.

facts.statement: The species name tanneri is named after Nathan Eldon Tanner, the first counselor of the First Presidency of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie tanneri, se debe al primer consejero de la Primera Presidencia de la Iglesia de Jesucristo de los Santos de los Últimos Días, Nathan Eldon Tanner.

facts.statement: The species Torvosaurus gurneyi is dedicated to the paleoartist James Gurney.
facts.quote: Torvosaurus gurneyi por su parte está dedicado al paleoartista James Gurney.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Edmarka rex and "Brontoraptor" truly belong to T. tanneri, as they lack detailed analysis to verify this.
facts.quote: Además, tanto Edmarka rex como "Brontoraptor" carecen de un análisis detallado para verificar si realmente pertenecen a T. tanneri.

facts.statement: Many researchers consider Edmarka rex and "Brontoraptor" to be part of Torvosaurus tanneri.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, muchos investigadores consideran a estos especímenes como parte de Torvosaurus tanneri.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the fewer upper jaw teeth in T. gurneyi are a real distinction or a conservation artifact, as the exact number of teeth in the complete maxilla cannot currently be determined.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, un examen posterior de un nuevo maxilar derecho probablemente perteneciente al mismo individuo que el holotipo de T. gurneyi ha determinado que si bien las dos especies se pueden distinguir en función de la morfología de la pared medial maxilar y las placas interdentales, el número supuestamente menor de dientes maxilares en la forma portuguesa puede ser un artefacto de conservación ya que no es posible saberlo en este momento. el número exacto de dientes en el maxilar completo.

facts.statement: Torvosaurus was originally described in 1979 and classified as a megalosaurid.
facts.quote: Cuando fue descrito originalmente en 1979, Torvosaurus fue clasificdo como un megalosáurido

facts.statement: In 1990, Ralph Molnar and colleagues assigned Torvosaurus to Carnosauria.
facts.quote: Fue luego asignado a Carnosauria por Ralph Molnar et al. en 1990

facts.statement: In 2003, Oliver Walter Mischa Rauhut placed Torvosaurus in a basal position within Spinosauroidea.
facts.quote: y a una posición basal en Spinosauroidea por Oliver Walter Mischa Rauhut en 2003

facts.statement: In 1994, Thomas Holtz assigned Torvosaurus to a very basal position in Tetanurae.

facts.statement: In 1985, Jensen classified Torvosaurus in its own family, Torvosauridae.
facts.quote: En 1985, Jensen asignó a Torvosaurus en su propia familia, los Torvosauridae

facts.statement: Although closely related to Megalosaurus, Torvosaurus appears to be more advanced or apomorphic.
facts.quote: Aunque es un pariente cercano de Megalosaurus, Torvosaurus parece ser más avanzado o apomórfico

facts.statement: The parent group of Torvosaurus is Megalosaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Megalosaurinae

facts.statement: Torvosaurus belongs to the family Megalosauridae.

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Torvosaurus is Torvosaurus tanneri.
facts.quote: Type species: Torvosaurus tanneri

facts.statement: Torvosaurus lived from the Callovian to the Tithonian stages, between 165.3 and 143.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Callovian to Tithonian (165.3 to 143.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: The discovery of Torvosaurus eggs was made in 2005 by the Dutch amateur fossil hunter Aart Walen.
facts.quote: Este descubrimiento fue realizado en 2005 por el buscador de fósiles holandés aficionado Aart Walen

facts.statement: The discovery of Torvosaurus eggs supports the idea that large theropod dinosaurs were oviparous.
facts.quote: Este descubrimiento da mayor apoyo a la idea de que los grandes dinosaurios terópodos eran ovíparos

facts.statement: This specimen represents the first evidence of a single-layered eggshell in theropod dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Representa la primera evidencia de una cáscara de huevo de una capa en los dinosaurios terópodos

facts.statement: The non-perturbed taphonomic environment and low-energy geological context corroborate that the eggs were buried for incubation.
facts.quote: Esto también es corroborado por el entorno tafonómico no perturbado y el contexto geológico de baja energía

facts.statement: It is unknown whether Torvosaurus provided parental care to its eggs and young or abandoned them shortly after laying, as the eggs were found abandoned due to unknown circumstances.

facts.statement: All documented Torvosaurus specimens from the Morrison Formation are likely adult individuals of similar size.

facts.statement: Torvosaurus may have experienced Type B1 population survival, characterized by increased mortality after reaching sexual maturity, as seen in other dinosaurs.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Torvosauridae is a valid family, as Torvosaurus is closely related to, and possibly the sister species of, the oldest Megalosaurus within Megalosaurinae.
